svg.text: One Google Cloud project, europe-west3. Every Cloud Run service is private, deployed --no-allow-unauthenticated.
The sealed exam has exactly one entry in its access
list, and that list is hashed into the chain. Granting
the Proposer access later breaks the chain instead
7 agents, each with a chain root
the Copilot writes the row, the console does not
refused, and recorded as a link
Screening runs before the policy, because the policy can key on its verdict.
ma_verdict is a predicate in the policy DSL, so a turn that was not screened is not the same as one that screened clean. When a policy keys on
screening and Model Armor is unavailable, the call is refused with SCREENING-UNAVAILABLE rather than allowed.
Two guarantees sit outside this code: BigQuery IAM produces the 403, a Cloud Storage retention lock refuses the owner’s delete. infra/70_prove_seal.sh and
infra/71_prove_immutability.sh assert them, and exit non-zero if either stops holding. Icons are stylised in Google Cloud’s palette, not the official set.
